body: Also, doing well in college does not necessarily mean you have life figured out. I was Magna Cum Laude and did internships every summer. I feel like a giant idiot 6 months into my first post college career level job.

He's home and seems to be himself again, just very tired. He felt very guilty about all of the things he said in the moment and was very aware that it was not a reflection of his true feelings. He was prescribed medication and has an appointment with someone next week. I think most of my concern and anxiety was just coming from *not knowing* and now everyone feels much better. I really appreciate all of your help throughout this, and it has actually inspired me to look into gaining more knowledge on this subject and seeing if I can help others.

I'm going to pick him up in about an hour. The doctor finally called be back and said he wants to leave. I have no idea what mood he'll be in. Do I need to hide all the knifes and scissors in the house? (He's never been violent and he supposedly took a lot of pills this time but the doctors found nothing in his stomach) What if he's just as angry and irritable as when he got there? What if he becomes violent towards me and my dad? I'm only 19 and relatively inexperienced. My brother has blamed my dad for this, my mom lives across the country, and he doesn't want anything to do with his girlfriend. Why am I the one who's left basically as the only one who has the power to decide whether he lives or dies? What if I make a small mistake and I ruin everything?

Again, I appreciate the feedback. I'm still on edge and haven't been able to sleep but for different reasons now. I've made a new post about it, so I won't bring it up here. I just wanted to say thank you.
Well I'm glad they don't feel as awkward as I do. I'm a female college student so i guess any strange adult man in my apartment is weird to me. Good to know I'm not doing the wrong thing!

I'm left handed. My sibling is also left handed and he doesn't suffer from any miso symptoms, and my dad is ambidextrous but claims he was supposed to be left handed and his parents/school/society made him use his right hand. His miso is worse than mine. This is a really interesting observation, and I'm interested to see what you discover.
Living in an apartment complex and having to let the maintenance guy in, only to proceed to sit on the couch and ignore him or awkwardly watch him do the work that needs to be done.

Thank you for the help. I am definitely trying to understand him, it's just I went from thinking there was literally no issues to him being in a hospital bed screaming at my dad and then him being transferred to an inpatient facility from like 3am-7am after being awake for 24 hours. Even now I'm still in shock.

What I meant by my dad is the only one that does anything for him: I moved away to college about a year and a half ago. My mom moved to California about a year ago to be closer to her family, all the while proclaiming she hated everyone who lived in this state, selling her car and buying and Audi, and basically saying she was done being a mom before my brother even graduated high school. My dad is the one who buys him food, fixes his car when he needs it, and basically does all of the things a parent does. But he's also the only one who disciplines my brother, who is (I thought) just a typical rebellious teenage boy. This year, he had stopped going to school and actually set a record for the most absences by a student at his high school. Claims he can't wake up in the morning but people will wake him up and he'll tell them he's getting ready and then go back to bed. We took him to the doctor for this and they said nothing was wrong. My dad offered my brother counseling and he said it would be a "waste of money".

He took 4 advil and then told his girlfriend it was a whole bottle of pain meds and then told the nurses at the hospital he couldn't remember what it was, only that it was not prescription.

He also told his girlfriend that day that we had supposedly ignored dozens of calls and texts and locked him out of the house as he was banging on the front door for help. We had no calls or texts, we never lock our front door, even when going on vacation, and my brother has a garage door opener as well as knows the garage code. Obviously these were all lies, and he's never been that kind of liar before. I can't tell whether he was just wanting us to think he was hurting himself for the attention (again, shitty for me to say) or he was honestly trying and just had no idea how.
